newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania OTC market ends firmer, seen keeping mood.
newsitem.headline: Romania OTC market ends firmer, seen keeping mood.

text.p: Romania's over-the-counter (OTC) market ended firmer on Thursday in active foreign and local buying.
Traders expected prices to rise further under strong demand, especially from foreign portfolio investors encouraged by recent improved investment legislation.

"The market is very atractive to foreigners and we see more capital inflows pouring into the market in the months ahead," a broker said. Cyclical corrections are expected, but, generally, the market will keep the uptrend until end-1997, he added.
"The metallurgical, oil and cement sectors were at centre-stage and will stay there," said a trader.
Operators said the recent firming of the leu over the past days had failled to impress foreign investors.
"Most stocks are cheap and a firmer leu has not affected buying decisions yet," one said. "The market takes three or four days to react of such moves."
On Thursday, gainers led losers by 122 to 98, while prices of 289 stocks were flat.

Three independent indices, computed by brokerage houses on the basis of average prices and market capitalisation, soared from Wednesday's session. VAB-RA grew by 4.7 percent to 4,503 points, BIG-OTC rose by 6.04 percent to 3,516.5 and CAS-RQ was up 5.9 percent at 805 points.
Oil refinery Arpechim was in focus on Thursday when a special deal struck outside the market pushed up its closing price by 800 lei to 33,000.
Another refinery, Petromidia, was 2,500 lei up at 36,500.
Cement maker Romcim firmed 500 lei to 93,500 in late trading. Traders said there was room for further slight rises.
Steel mill Sidex went up 1,100 lei closing at 19,100, under continous buying pressure, traders said.
Traders said interest in Otelinox, another steel mill, was on the rise on expectations of a move to the Bucharest stock exchange early next month. The company gained 1,000 lei to a 35,500 close.
Overall, turnover rose to 25.23 billion lei from 15.32 billion on Wednesday.
